text:
sami: I opened a tiny PR to unify streaming + pagination snippets across py/ts/go. link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/507. Goals: use empty string as canonical cursor start, show per-request deadline patterns, and add a 1-row knob cheat-sheet. please quick review.
jules: skimmed. prefer async iterator in python and context timeout in go. also call out that resume tokens are opaque.
lee: TS snippet should show AbortController + note that abort may still emit final partial event from server. added small example.
sami: pushed updates: py uses `async for` with `asyncio.wait_for`, go uses `context.WithTimeout`, ts uses `AbortController`. normalized `cursor: ""` everywhere and added a tiny "knob -> effect" line: batching -> throughput up, per-request deadline -> bounded latency, ttl cache -> reduce cold-start.
docs-bot: PR 507 updated: snippets compile checks passed.
jules: one nit: change wording in FAQ to "resume tokens are opaque; treat as cursors", then :shipit:.
sami: done. merging in 15m unless there's any objection. thanks!
